text:
Zara Khan: Hey team, Zara here — second day. On M1 Mac and trying to finalize dev bootstrap. Two small but annoying blockers: 

1) `brew` shows some packages installed under /usr/local (intel) and others under /opt/homebrew (arm). When I run `asdf install nodejs 18.16.0` it picks a wrong openssl path and fails to build.
2) My dotfiles bootstrap replaces my existing ~/.gitconfig unexpectedly. The script said it would back up but didn’t.

What should I do? Steps I ran:
```
brew install asdf direnv openssl@1.1
git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/dotfiles.git ~/dotfiles
~/dotfiles/bootstrap.sh
asdf plugin-add nodejs
asdf install nodejs 18.16.0
```

Leo (DevEx): welcome Zara! :wave: a couple of pointers we give new hires on arm macs: 
- Homebrew on M1 should be under /opt/homebrew; if you previously had Rosetta brew installs they live in /usr/local. Prefer one prefix. To force builds to use arm homebrew binaries, run shells without Rosetta and `eval $(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)`.
- For asdf + openssl builds export flags so compile picks Homebrew openssl: 
```
export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/include"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib/pkgconfig"
```
Then retry `asdf install`.

Nina Park: re: dotfiles, our bootstrap is supposed to create backups under `~/.dotfiles_backup_YYYYMMDD`. Can you `ls -la` the home dir and check if a backup exists? If the script overwrote your `~/.gitconfig` it might be because the bootstrap detected a previously incomplete run. You can restore from the backup or from the repo: `cp ~/dotfiles/templates/gitconfig ~/.gitconfig` (we keep a sanitized template).

Zara Khan: I checked — there is a `~/.dotfiles_backup_20260315` with my old gitconfig. Restored it, thanks. After exporting the openssl flags `asdf install` progressed further but failed on a GPG key step for node. The asdf-nodejs import script errors with `gpg: no valid OpenPGP data found`.

Leo (DevEx): for that plugin run: 
```
# ensure gpg is installed
brew install gpg
# run import script from asdf plugin
bash ~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring
# sometimes you need to refresh keys:
gpg --keyserver hkps://keys.openpgp.org --recv-keys 4ED778F539E3634C779C87C6D7062848A1AB005C
```
If it still fails, try running the import under Rosetta if you previously used intel-installed gpg. But typically installing gpg under /opt/homebrew and running the import fixes it.

Zara Khan: Installed gpg via Homebrew under /opt/homebrew and re-ran import - that fixed it. Node installed. One last tiny question: I use fish shell. Some of our onboarding scripts assume POSIX `source ~/.profile`. Any recommended quick compatibility tips?

Nina Park: fish is fine but many scripts expect sh/zsh. We usually tell new hires either switch to zsh temporarily or add this to `~/.config/fish/config.fish` to source POSIX profiles: 
```
# simple compat: run bash to source sh-style files
if test -f $HOME/.profile
  bash -lc "source $HOME/.profile"
end
```
Or use `bass` to import env vars. If you want, we can pair and ensure your fish config sources asdf and direnv hooks.

Dotfiles Bot: Canonical dotfiles + arm mac notes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dotfiles (see docs/mac-arm.md). If you notice a script bug open an issue in that repo and tag @dev-ex.

Zara Khan: Thanks all — env now matches prod for node and gitconfig restored. Will ping if anything else pops up. :tada:
